title: First cohomology local system of a smooth projective curve family
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $g\geq0$ an integer, and $\ell$ a prime invertible in every local ring of $T$. Put $A=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$. Let $f:X\to T$ be a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Suppose every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is a geometrically connected curve of genus $g$: explicitly, for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $X_{\bar t}$ is a connected smooth projective curve of dimension one with $\dim_\Omega H^1(X_{\bar t},\mathcal O_{X_{\bar t}})=g$ [def-sc-genus]. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], set $H=R^1f_*\underline A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], as a sheaf of $\underline A_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $H$ is etale locally isomorphic to $\underline{A^{2g}}_T$. For every morphism $v:T'\to T$, with $X'=X\times_TT'$ and $f':X'\to T'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the canonical degree-one proper-base-change map
$$\mathrm{BC}^1_v:v^{-1}H\xrightarrow{\sim}R^1f'_*\underline A_{X'}$$
is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. In particular $H_{\bar t}\cong H^1((X_{\bar t})_{\mathrm{et}},\underline A)$ has dimension $2g$ over $A$, with the stalk identification induced by this base-change map [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. No Noetherian hypothesis or choice of a root of unity on $T$ is required; $g=0$, $\ell=2$, disconnected $T$ and empty $T$ are included.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], the specified projective-bundle convention makes $f$ proper, without a Noetherian assumption. The constant coefficient sheaf $\underline A_X$ is already locally constant with one-dimensional fibre over the field $A$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-proper-finite-cohomology-local-system] with $S=T$, $F=\underline A_X$ and $q=1$: $f$ is smooth and proper and $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. Thus $H$ is etale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-vector-space local models.

source.place: Tag 0GLI, proposition-loc-cst-torsion; properness: morphisms.tex Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper

proof.text: For arbitrary $v:T\!\prime\to T$, apply [det-properbasechange-modules] with $\Lambda=A$ and $K=\underline A_X[0]$. Its underlying cohomology is killed by $\ell$, hence torsion. It gives an isomorphism for the specified derived exchange, not merely an unspecified comparison. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], inverse image on constant-coefficient modules is exact, and by [lem-kun-pullback-constant] the pulled-back coefficient sheaf is canonically $\underline A_{X\!\prime}$. Taking degree-one cohomology therefore gives exactly the asserted $\mathrm{BC}^1_v$ isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 095T, theorem-proper-base-change; the module exchange comparison is det-properbasechange-modules

proof.text: In Step 2 take $v=\bar t:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], global sections on $P$ are exact and $\Gamma(P,\bar t^{-1}H)=H_{\bar t}$. To identify the other side, compute $Rf_{\bar t*}\underline A$ with an injective resolution $I^\bullet$ as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Exactness of $\Gamma(P,-)$ gives $\Gamma(P,\mathcal H^1(f_{\bar t*}I^\bullet))=H^1(\Gamma(P,f_{\bar t*}I^\bullet))=H^1(\Gamma(X_{\bar t},I^\bullet))$. This last group is $H^1((X_{\bar t})_{\mathrm{et}},\underline A)$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The identifications are $A$-linear, since all maps commute with scalar endomorphisms. This constructs the required stalk identification from the same base-change map.

source.place: Tags 04JN, remark-stalk-pullback, and 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point; degree one of Tag 095T

proof.text: The hypothesis says that $X_{\bar t}$ is a connected smooth projective curve over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$, with genus $g$. It is proper by base change of the proper $f$, using [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The image of $\ell$ in $\Omega$ is a unit, so $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}\Omega$. Choose a primitive $\ell$-th root in this field using [lem-sc-primitive-root] and apply [thm-sc-proper-cohomology] with $n=\ell$. It gives $H^1((X_{\bar t})_{\mathrm{et}},\underline A)\cong A^{2g}$. Even if this isomorphism is initially read as additive, it is $A$-linear: every scalar is represented by an integer and additive homomorphisms commute with integer multiplication. Together with Step 3 this gives $\dim_A H_{\bar t}=2g$. No root on the base $T$ has been chosen.

Choose a trivializing etale cover from Step 1, with $H|_U\cong\underline V_U$. Discard empty members. On a nonempty member choose a geometric point $\bar u$ and let $\bar t$ be its image on $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], the stalk of $H|_U$ at $\bar u$ is $H_{\bar t}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], it is also $V$. Step 4 identifies this finite-dimensional $A$-vector space with $A^{2g}$. Applying that linear isomorphism to the constant sheaves gives $H|_U\cong\underline{A^{2g}}_U$ on every member. For empty $T$ the empty etale cover suffices. This proves the local rank assertion also for disconnected $T$; the same argument gives the zero sheaf when $g=0$ and works unchanged for $\ell=2$.
